doc.title: Norris Turney interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997

title: Player piano and radio big bands in Ohio
summary: He heard blues on the family player piano, then big bands on the radio: Henderson, Hines, Basie, Lunceford.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: In growing up in Ohio, was that a part of the music that you heard as a child?
Did your parents have blues recordings, or where did you hear most of your music?

At the player piano. And we had some blues on that. And then we got a radio. And we used to listen to big bands, Fletcher Henderson, Earl Hines, Basie when he first went to New York, and all the big bands you know, Jimmie Lunceford.
Radio was a huge part of the way information was spread at the time, right?
